elements.note: Painted hardwood pelmet boxing the sliding track, called out on doors 2, 3 and 4. Door 1 (aluminium) does not get one.

warnings: *** THE DOOR SCHEDULE, AND IT SETTLES HALF THE OPENING-MARK AMBIGUITY CARRIED SINCE A-05. *** There are exactly FIVE door marks, 1 to 5. Any circled mark 6 seen on the plans and elevations therefore CANNOT be a door -- it must be a window. A-23 should confirm.
EVERY DOOR IS 2.05 M HIGH without exception. Widths are 3.10 / 0.80 / 1.10 / 1.10 / 0.90.

*** DOOR 2 IS 0.80 M WIDE, BELOW THE 0.90 M CLEAR WIDTH THE A-03 UNIVERSAL-DESIGN BRIEF SETS ('มีขนาดกว้างอย่างน้อย 90 ซม'). *** It serves the upper-floor bathroom, which is the storey the brief itself says is for occupants without mobility problems -- so it is probably deliberate, but the drawing does not say so. Flagged here rather than silently accepted.
MATERIALS SPLIT CLEANLY: door 1 is white powder-coated ALUMINIUM with 6 mm green tinted glass; doors 2-5 are all UPVC. That matches A-02, which specifies both systems.

FOUR OF THE FIVE DOORS SLIDE. Only door 5 is a swing leaf, and it is the only one given the lever handle ('มือจับชนิดก้านโยก') that A-02 and A-03 require. The sliders get 'ชุดรางเลื่อนพร้อมอุปกรณ์ล็อคและมือจับสแตนเลส มาตรฐานครบชุด'. A-03's preference for sliding doors is clearly followed.
A painted hardwood pelmet 3/4"x4" boxes the sliding track on doors 2, 3 and 4 but not on the aluminium door 1 -- a small item easy to miss in a take-off.
The ลูกฟัก (panel/glazing) row is left BLANK for doors 2, 4 and 5. That is as printed; no glazing is specified for them.
Level tags show where each door is used: doors 1 and 5 on both floors (+0.40 and +3.40), doors 3 and 4 on the ground floor only, door 2 upstairs only.
